title: Throwback Nissan Pathfinder SE-V6? Yes, Please!

body_markdown:
The annual Las Vegas show put on by the Specialty Equipment Marketing Association[(SEMA)](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/sema/) never fails to attract wild concepts from both independent shops and OEMs alike. Nissan is no exception, and as it prepares to[relaunch the Xterra](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/nissan-will-revive-the-xterra-in-2028/) nameplate in 2028, the carmaker is showcasing its off-roading chops with a trio of 4×4 builds based on the Pathfinder and Armada SUVs, as well as the Frontier pickup truck.


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


The Pathfinder XE-V6 concept sports a throwback look to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Nissan’s original SUV. Retro XE-V6 graphics recall the era of the celebrated WD21-based truck, with its 3.0-liter V-6—a precursor to the 284-horsepower V-6 powering today’s Pathy (with 295 on tap in Rock Creek editions). The concept boasts a four-inch suspension lift to fit its prototype 18-inch NISMO AX-5 wheels shod with 285/75R18 Yokohama Geolandar mud tires. Custom tube bumpers and rock sliders frame the perimeter of the SUV, with an integrated Warn winch up front, a swing-out tire carrier at the rear, skid plates underneath, and a beefy rack up top, from which hang Molle panels. It’s the kind of overlanding build you’d expect to encounter deep in the wilds.


Armada Jungle Patrol


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


Meanwhile, with its full-sized Armada SUV, Nissan has gone with a safari theme in the “Jungle Patrol” show car. As the current Armada is based on Nissan’s unstoppable Patrol, the theme is fitting, and it includes a chopped roof replaced with a tubular cage, with a bevy of NISMO lights across the front. It has a widened track, with a long-travel suspension cushioning 37-inch Yokohamas on NISMO Axis beadlock wheels, and the matte black paintwork includes stark red accents vaguely reminiscent of animal scratches. The truck’s 425-hp V-6 runs through a prototype NISMO cat-back exhaust.


Nissan Frontier RONIN


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


Finally, Nissan says the Frontier RONIN concept represents its “vision for a high-performance, unstoppable off-road truck.” The name is a reference to the masterless samurai warriors of feudal Japan, and in this guise the truck speaks to the concept’s go-anywhere intent. Underhood is a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter V-6, while the suspension largely comes from the full-size Titan, which provides four inches of lift and widens the track by 12 inches. The “Titan swap” has long been a popular mod in the Xterra community, so it’s fun to see Nissan tackle it in Frontier-land. All of which helps this Frontier sit confidently on 35-inch Yokohama Geolandars with 17-inch NISMO Ascend beadlock wheels. Tube bumpers, rock sliders, and skid plates provide plenty of exterior protection.


None of the three concepts are in Nissan’s product pipeline, but that doesn’t mean we won’t see some of these features available down the road. The NISMO catalog is vast, after all, and the features found in the carmaker’s current Rock Creek packages for the Pathfinder, Rogue, and Kicks can be traced to past SEMA concepts.


Nissan


Nissan has long prided itself on the durability of its truck lineup, and this trio shines a spotlight on that belief. “Capability, confidence, and off-road excitement have been core parts of the Nissan brand for decades, from rugged daily drivers to iconic desert racing victories and beyond,” says Kim Less, vice president of Aftersales and Customer Loyalty for Nissan Americas. “As we look toward a future of even more capable trucks and SUVs, including an all-new Xterra, these SEMA Show concepts allow builders to unleash their creativity, while also exploring ideas and innovations that can help inform the direction for accessorizing future Nissan trucks and SUVs.”


Nissan faithful would love to see many of these features made available for the current lineup. How the company responds to those wishes will be a big indicator of its future commitment to the off-roading community that believes in its trucks and SUVs.
